basis: Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive sterile arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne and hidradenitis suppurativa.
Oral, digital/skeletal and CNS malformations define the syndrome; cardiac septal hypertrophy is also a defining feature, meeting the diagnostic-feature exception.
BAAT-related bile acid conjugation disorder with jaundice in 7/7 and elevated transaminases in 3/7; rickets in 2/7 is below 30%.
Congenital ventricular septal malformation involving the infundibular septum.
Bacteroidaceae bacterial infection umbrella; no single anatomical site is consistently affected across the group.
Inherited vitreoretinopathy affecting retinal vascular development and vitreoretinal structure.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy from defective sphingolipid biosynthesis; ulcers are secondary neuropathic injuries and osteomyelitis is a separate infection.
Defined by cerebrovascular malformations, pulmonary arterial hypertension and lymphedema; vascular location alone does not establish brain or lung tissue damage.
Benign smooth muscle tumour arising in the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Otofacial and cervical/shoulder skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; cochlear hypoplasia and mixed hearing loss are documented. High palate alone adds no GI damage.
Skeletal malformation syndrome characterized by bowed long bones and limb abnormalities.
GATAD1-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ventricular function and heart failure.
CD40L immunodeficiency; neutropenia in 39/62 (~63%) and oral ulceration in 25/56 (~45%). Infections are separate diseases; sclerosing cholangitis occurs in <30%.
Amino acid transport disorder defined by hypercalcemia and nephrocalcinosis; diarrhea alone does not establish gastrointestinal tissue damage.
Neoplasm occupying the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis; other tumour origins vary across this umbrella.
Male reproductive system disease umbrella; reproductive organs have no axis, and endocrine or urinary dysfunction is not intrinsic to the group.
Abnormal coordination of oculomotor and abducens innervation defines the disorder, with ocular motility dysfunction and ptosis in 4/5 patients.
Familial Behcet-like autoinflammation characteristically includes recurrent oral mucosal ulceration; other organ damage is insufficiently consistent across subtypes.
Localized nodular inflammation of the episclera; an associated autoimmune disease is not required and does not establish an immune mechanism for every case.
Inherited myxomatous mitral valve disease causing prolapse and regurgitation.
Multiple meningiomas arising from spinal meninges; tumour origin belongs to the neurologic axis.
Spastic paraplegia and neuropathy with optic atrophy in 21/22; lasting joint contractures occur in 80-99% and scoliosis/kyphosis in 14/22 (~64%).
Intellectual and global developmental impairment define the disorder; sensorineural hearing loss affects 12/21 (~57%). Other structural organ findings are below 30%.
Spinal muscular atrophy is a motor neuron disorder; accompanying intellectual disability also belongs to the neurologic axis.
Benign inverted papilloma arising from respiratory mucosa of the ethmoid sinus; sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
